name: The Ledger of Ashes

stars.name: Ledger
stars.notes: Ancient, even-tempered orange dwarf whose wide-spaced planetary family survived eons of stellar drift nearly intact.

planets.name: Folio
planets.notes: Heat-cured rock used as the innermost survey benchmark.

planets.name: Vellum
planets.notes: Smooth, pale surface scoured by micrometeorite flows; consortium probes mapped it twice and moved on.

planets.name: Marginalia
planets.notes: Cold, thin-aired terrestrial at the system's habitable margin; flagged as a possible second settlement site if the founding takes.

planets.name: Redaction
planets.notes: Ochre dunes over permafrost; automated weather relays were installed here during the first survey season.

planets.name: Incunabula
planets.notes: First of two giants; its upper atmosphere is a scheduled helium-3 skim stop on the outbound tanker route.

planets.name: Palimpsest
planets.notes: Airless world whose surface bears overlapping crater generations that surveyors nicknamed the corrections.

planets.name: Rubric
planets.notes: Dominant giant with a deep red band; its shepherded moons anchor the outer belt's inner edge.

planets.name: Colophon
planets.notes: Ring-shepherding ice world whose largest moon, Imprimatur, hosts the consortium's founding station.

planets.name: Ashleaf
planets.notes: Cracked glacial shell with cryovolcanic plumes visible from orbit on clear passes.

planets.name: Erratum
planets.notes: Tilted far off the system plane by an ancient encounter; its odd orbit is a favorite navigation exercise for consortium pilots.

planets.name: Flyleaf
planets.notes: Dim final entry in the catalogue, unvisited since its discovery pass.

asteroid_belts.name: The Interleaf Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Rock-and-metal shoal staked with consortium assay markers ahead of any future extraction license.

asteroid_belts.name: The Cold Index
asteroid_belts.notes: Sparse volatile-rich ring of debris; surveyed as a water feedstock source for the Colophon settlement project.

stations.name: Imprimatur Founding Station
stations.location: orbit of Imprimatur, moon of planet 8
stations.notes: Pre-fabricated colony head being assembled above Colophon's largest moon; no planetary settlement exists yet anywhere in the system.

stations.name: Ashleaf Survey Platform
stations.notes: Corporate science platform cataloguing plume chemistry and belt composition to justify the colony charter's next renewal.

faction_control.notes: The consortium holds exclusive development charter under an old imperial grant it keeps framed in the station mess; no other faction maintains a presence.

history: Long dismissed as an empty orange dwarf, the system was re-surveyed by the Palewater Consortium and selected for a staged colonization venture.
The Imprimatur Founding Station was emplaced three years ago; construction has proceeded slowly against supply shortfalls and one winter-long comms blackout.
The consortium's colonial board meets quarterly by relay, and each meeting has deferred the decision to land the first settlers.
description: An ancient orange star presides over eleven worlds spaced so widely that whole orbits fall dark between one port call and the next. Rocky planets huddle near the dim warmth while the true mass of the system lies outward: two great gas giants, a scatter of ice worlds, and twin belts of debris writing quiet margins around them all. Everything is cold, orderly, and patient.

The Palewater Consortium is betting the system's future on a colony that does not yet exist, assembling the Imprimatur Founding Station above Colophon's principal moon while its scientists inventory plumes, belts, and ore assays. Light traffic serves the project alone: tankers skimming Incunabula, freighters feeding the station, and survey launches crossing the long dark between entries. No world here is inhabited, and the consortium's paperwork insists that is a temporary condition.

Station crews whisper that the founding has been deferred so many times because the original imperial grant names conditions no one can verify anymore. The Ashleaf platform's plume findings have been forwarded but never acknowledged, and the board's minutes remain sealed even to senior staff. A newcomer with capital, or with patience, may yet learn what the consortium is truly waiting to write into the empty ledger.
